messages.text:
"Create a simple mobile ASMR music looper game inspired by Teenage Engineering design.

Key Features:
- UI Style: Clean, minimalist, muted pastel colors, and physical-looking buttons inspired by the OP-1.
- Beatpad Grid: A grid of selectable squares, each playing a seamlessly looping ASMR sound (Rain, Wind, Birds, Crumpled Paper, Bubbles, Vinyl Crackle).
- Multi-Select Looper: Tap a square to toggle its sound loop on or off. Players can select multiple squares at once to layer sounds together.
- Audio Sync: All active sound loops automatically stay synced to the same tempo grid.
- Control Knobs: Include simple UI knobs to adjust Reverb, Delay, and Master Speed/BPM.
- Visuals: Soft, pastel animations on the screen react and pulse smoothly in real-time as sounds play.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable mobile ASMR music looper game with a minimalist, muted-pastel physical-instrument aesthetic inspired by Teenage Engineering’s OP-1.

## Requirements
- Six toggleable looping sounds: Rain, Wind, Birds, Crumpled Paper, Bubbles, and Vinyl Crackle; allow multiple layers and keep active sounds tempo-synced.
- Include Reverb, Delay, and Master Speed/BPM knobs, plus smooth sound-reactive pastel visuals.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks (viewport at most 1280px wide); read only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a PNG.

## Decisions
- Implemented a standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript app with generated Web Audio sounds rather than external audio assets.
- Built a custom visual identity named “softloop,” with animated visualizer, quantized sound toggles, keyboard-accessible controls, and responsive mobile layout.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added full UI, responsive styling, six sound pads, Web Audio loop synthesis, beat scheduler, effect/tempo controls, master mute, and help modal.
- Checked desktop and mobile layouts with screenshots; verified a pad toggles on and updates the active count.
- `node --check app.js` completed successfully.
- Added an empty data favicon to avoid the browser’s favicon 404.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Optionally re-run browser checks after the favicon change; screenshots are in the ignored `screenshots/` directory.
2. Summarize the finished implementation and assumptions to the user.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: App structure and controls.
- `styles.css`: Responsive instrument UI, animations, and styling.
- `app.js`: Audio synthesis, synchronization, interactions, and controls.
- `screenshots/softloop-mobile.jpg`: Latest mobile screenshot.
- `screenshots/softloop-check.jpg`: Earlier desktop screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- A local HTTP server was started on port 3002 for browser testing.
- Playwright verified mobile document width 375px against a 390px viewport.

Built **softloop**, a playable, responsive ASMR music looper in `index.html`, `styles.css`, and `app.js`.

It includes six toggleable sound layers, beat-quantized starts and accents, Reverb/Delay/Tempo knobs, master mute, and an animated sound visualizer. Audio is synthesized in the browser, so no external sound files are needed; tap a pad to start playback.

Verified the app in desktop and mobile browser viewports, confirmed a pad toggles on, and checked `app.js` syntax. Mobile content fits without horizontal overflow. Screenshots are saved in the ignored `screenshots/` directory.

**Assumption:** ambient textures loop continuously, while their accents join the shared tempo grid.
